story: Gary and Donna are out on Magnolia Loop under a clear, breezy sky at 9:17 on Thursday night, with Gary cheerfully promising to help Donna hand out a few flyers before they call it a night by ten. Donna is marching ahead toward the Rec Center with real determination, while Hal is dutifully counting the pink plastic flamingos in view against the L-02 limit so the street stays within the rules. Back at her house, Rosa is content in her kitchen, marinating the pork and sorting her grocery list for Friday's errands.
events: Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the flamingos visible from the street against the L-02 limit
Rosa (rosa kitchen): Prep what I can tonight: marinate the pork and sort the grocery list by Friday errands

gary.thought_process: Hal and I are square, so no need to repeat myself to him. Donna has asked me once already to head to the rec center for the ladder match prep, and I told her back at tick 83 I'd partner with her. It's past nine at night, though, and the courts are one thing, but I still have the golf cart project waiting on approval. Nothing to do on that front but wait. Standing around chatting won't move anything forward, and Donna's waiting on an answer. I'll tell her I'm in and head over to the rec center to hit some third-shot drops. Keeps my word and keeps me useful to my partner.

parameters.content: Alright, Donna, lead the way. I'll hit a few drops with you, but we're done by ten or Hal'll have my hide. Hal, Saturday's a date, save me a plate of that cornbread.

donna.thought_process: I already told Gary at tick 160 to head over to the rec center for third-shot drops, and he's now chatting with Hal about his paperwork. No need to repeat the invitation. It's past 9 PM, courts are probably nearly done for the night, and I'm the one who wants us ready for the ladder match. Best thing to move things forward is to actually go to the rec center myself, so Gary follows when he's done with Hal. I can also reserve a court slot if one is open, keeping within the 2-hour limit.

parameters.content: Heading to the rec center to grab a court and get some practice in before the ladder match; Gary can catch up once he's done with Hal.

hal.thought_process: Gary already told me the paperwork is filed, and I said we're square. Saturday is settled, cornbread and good chair. Nothing left to say to him. Donna's flamingo flock is right here, though, and L-02 caps visible ornaments at three. My earlier notice on the bulletin board says the count is under review, so I ought to actually look at the flock and count by the book. Fair is fair: count first, then decide whether to file anything. Let the two of them head off to their pickleball.

parameters.content: Count the flamingos visible from the street against the L-02 limit

rosa.thought_process: It's past 9 PM Thursday and I've already set the table, cards, menu plan, and checked my shift schedule. The only loose end is the grocery list I made at the kitchen last tick. Nobody's around, and everyone has committed to Saturday, so no need to chase anyone. I should do something useful with the hour: go over the kitchen prep, maybe pre-plan what can be cooked Friday so Saturday isn't a scramble, then get to bed since I'm tired and have errands tomorrow.

parameters.content: Prep what I can tonight: marinate the pork and sort the grocery list by Friday errands

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
